name: William Henry Harrison
blurb: 9th US President (1773–1841) · gave the longest inaugural address in history — nearly two hours, no coat — then died 31 days later, the shortest presidency ever
source: Wikimedia Commons: William Henry Harrison by James Reid Lambdin, 1835.jpg

name: Frank Lloyd Wright
blurb: Architect (1867–1959) · his Fallingwater cantilevers so far over a waterfall that the contractor secretly doubled Wright's rebar, likely saving it from collapse
source: Wikimedia Commons: Frank Lloyd Wright LC-USZ62-36384.jpg

name: Rudyard Kipling
blurb: Writer (1865–1936) · at 41 became the first English-language Nobel literature laureate — still the youngest ever
source: Wikimedia Commons: Kipling nd.jpg

name: Mary Magdalene
blurb: New Testament follower of Jesus (1st century AD) · her reputation as a reformed prostitute comes from a 6th-century sermon conflating three women, not scripture
source: Wikimedia Commons: Philippe de Champaigne - The Repentant Magdalen - Google Art Project.jpg

name: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi
blurb: Shah of Iran (1919–1980) · after the 1979 revolution he moved through six countries in eighteen months, dying of cancer with no permanent asylum
source: Wikimedia Commons: Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, 1973.jpg

name: Ferdinand Marcos
blurb: President and dictator of the Philippines (1917–1989) · when he fled in 1986, his wife Imelda left behind thousands of pairs of shoes, since displayed as a monument to the regime's excess
source: Wikimedia Commons: Lieutenant Ferdinand E. Marcos.jpg

name: Eleanor Roosevelt
blurb: First Lady and human rights campaigner (1884–1962) · held press conferences open only to female reporters, forcing newspapers to keep women on staff just to cover her
source: Wikimedia Commons: Eleanor Roosevelt at the United Nations, circa 1946-1947 (3x4 cropped).jpg

name: Ruhollah Khomeini
blurb: Supreme Leader of Iran (1902–1989) · led the 1979 revolution from exile in Paris, his sermons smuggled into Iran on cassette tapes
source: Wikimedia Commons: Ruhollah Khomeini portrait 2 (cropped).jpg

name: H. P. Lovecraft
blurb: Horror writer (1890–1937) · died in poverty and nearly unknown — his Cthulhu Mythos only became famous decades after his death
source: Wikimedia Commons: Howard Phillips Lovecraft.jpg

name: James A. Garfield
blurb: 20th US President (1831–1881) · Alexander Graham Bell built a metal detector to find the assassin's bullet, but the search failed — nobody thought to move him off his metal bed frame
attribution: Unknown; part of Brady-Handy Photograph Collection.
source: Wikimedia Commons: James Abram Garfield, photo portrait seated.jpg
image_author: Unknown; part of Brady-Handy Photograph Collection.

name: Ali
blurb: Fourth Rashidun caliph and cousin of Muhammad (601–661 AD) · Shia Islam holds him as the Prophet's rightful successor, the root of Islam's central schism
source: Wikimedia Commons: The ten to whom Paradise was promised (Ali).png

name: Idi Amin
blurb: Military dictator of Uganda (1925–2003) · his official title included 'Conqueror of the British Empire'; he also declared himself the uncrowned King of Scotland
source: Wikimedia Commons: Idi Amin at UN (United Nations, New York) gtfy.00132 (cropped).jpg

name: Timur
blurb: Turco-Mongol conqueror also called Tamerlane (1336–1405) · legend holds his tomb was cursed — Soviet archaeologists opened it in June 1941, two days before Germany invaded the USSR
source: Wikimedia Commons: Timur seated (earliest known portrait), Timurid genealogy, 1405-1409, Samarkand (TSMK, H2152).jpg

name: John the Baptist
blurb: Prophet who baptized Jesus in the Jordan (c. 1 BC – c. 30 AD) · beheaded at a birthday feast after Salome's dance, his head brought in on a platter
source: Wikimedia Commons: Accademia - St John the Baptist by Titian Cat314.jpg

name: Ayrton Senna
blurb: Formula One driver (1960–1994) · died leading at Imola with an Austrian flag in his cockpit, meant to honour a friend killed in practice the day before
source: Wikimedia Commons: Ayrton Senna 9 - Cropped.jpg

name: Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis
blurb: US First Lady, later a book editor (1929–1994) · spent her last two decades editing books at Viking and Doubleday, insisting on no special treatment
source: Wikimedia Commons: Jackie Kennedy Color Portrait (3x4 cropped).jpg

name: Shinzō Abe
blurb: Prime Minister of Japan (1954–2022) · Japan's longest-serving PM, assassinated with a homemade gun while giving a street speech
source: Wikimedia Commons: Shinzō Abe 2000.jpg

name: James Buchanan
blurb: 15th US President (1791–1868) · the only president who never married, and historians' perennial pick for the worst president in US history
source: Wikimedia Commons: James Buchanan (cropped).jpg

name: Douglas MacArthur
blurb: US Army general (1880–1964) · waded ashore in the Philippines for the cameras in 1944, then restaged the same shot at a later landing because reporters loved it
source: Wikimedia Commons: MacArthur Manila (cropped2).jpg

name: Akira Kurosawa
blurb: Film director (1910–1998) · filmed 'Seven Samurai's battles with multiple telephoto cameras so actors wouldn't know which one was rolling
source: Wikimedia Commons: Akirakurosawa-onthesetof7samurai-1953-page88.jpg

name: Robert F. Kennedy
blurb: US Attorney General and senator (1925–1968) · shot in a hotel kitchen pantry minutes after winning the 1968 California primary
source: Wikimedia Commons: Robert F. Kennedy.jpg

name: Muhammad Ali Jinnah
blurb: Founder of Pakistan (1876–1948) · secretly dying of tuberculosis throughout partition — only his sister and doctor knew before his death just over a year later
source: Wikimedia Commons: Jinnah1945c.jpg
